nonPoolDecisions: Reading: all ten questions are required; each printed (a)/(b) part is a 5-mark practice card. “3 mharc + 2 mharc” items are order-dependent (first correct point 3, second 2) and stay whole at 0/3/5; single answers with a printed partial (“= 3 mharc”) allow 0/3/5, otherwise 0/5.
Reading language: “Gaeilge lochtach: 0 - 5 a bhaint den iomlán a gnóthaíodh” is one deduction from each 50-mark passage total; cards state it without applying it inside a part.
Prescribed prose (2A): Dís, Oisín i dTír na nÓg and Hurlamaboc each print one 25-mark question (five points at 5 = 2 + 3); no sub-questions, so each stays one whole card.

Prescribed poetry (3A): each poem is a whole 25-mark card with (i) 8, (ii) 8, (iii) 9 and one 0–4 Gaeilge deduction; every printed sub-question is also a practice card at its own tariff. 3A(a)(i) prints three questions (a) 2, (b) 2, (c) 2 + 2: each is a practice slot (“Freagraí:” keys; (c) allows 0/2/4).

Literature mark values: other literature sub-questions keep the full range because the scheme’s points are indicative and further relevant points are credited “de réir a bhfiúntais”; the direct-quotation cap (“Línte cuí díreach … = 2 mharc + 2 mharc”) is guidance inside the award, not a separate route.
Optional prose (2B) and optional poetry (3B) stay whole: the text is open content chosen by the candidate, and the naming, theme, title and author marks belong to the whole answer.

Choose-two within 2A, 2B, 3A or 3B is a choice, not a route: each printed option keeps its own 25-mark card and carries the instruction in its task requirements; no two-option combination cards are published. The scheme marks each option on its own (no joint marking).
Q2A or Q2B and Q3A or Q3B are alternatives; Scheme lists of sample answers are indicative answer keys, not route pools.
The modified marking scheme (PDF 30) changes language assessment for eligible candidates, not the printed tasks.
sourceFindings: Paper 2 = 200: Léamhthuiscint A 50 + B 50 (five questions of 10, each (a) 5 + (b) 5), Prós 50 (two of three at 25), Filíocht 50 (two of three at 25).

Reading A “Na Cluichí Oilimpeacha agus Parailimpeacha, 2024” (paper pages 4–5, scheme PDF 15–16) and B “Páirc an Fhionnuisce” (paper 6–7, scheme PDF 17–18). Scheme A 1(b) prints the question as “…ar lasadh ann?” where the paper has “…ar lasadh istigh ann?”; cards use the paper wording.

Prescribed prose (paper 8): Dís, Oisín i dTír na nÓg, Hurlamaboc at 25. Optional prose (paper 9): (a) 23 (5,5,5,4,4) + 2 title and author; (b) 1 for naming the main character + 22 (5,5,4,4,4) + 2 title; (c) 1 for the main theme + 22 + 2 title and author.

Prescribed poetry (paper 10–12): Mo ghrá-sa (idir lúibíní), An tEarrach Thiar, Colscaradh at 8/8/9. Optional poetry (paper 13): (a) 9 (1 + 4 + 4) / 7 (1 + 3 + 3) / 7, (b) 9 / 7 / 7, (c) 9 (5 + 4) / 7 / 7, + 2 for poem and poet; the same poem may not be used twice.
Literature language: “[Gaeilge lochtach: 0-4 a bhaint den iomlán a gnóthaíodh]” after every literature route; it is a deduction from that route, never inside one sub-question.
The legacy cards marked every literature answer as one 25-mark Eolas block and every reading question as one 10-mark block; they now carry the printed part and sub-question tariffs.
